claims.statement: The lifecycle separates raw intake, normalized sources, AI-generated `_drafts/`, review verdicts, and canonical `concepts/`; the new-source process is prohibited from modifying `concepts/`, and candidates remain pending in `_drafts/` until review and promotion.

The new-source workflow preserves or completes a typed source directory with `meta.yaml`, `notes.md`, and `highlights.md`; it creates one to ten reviewable draft concepts, checks existing concepts and drafts for duplication, and records likely canonical overlap as an optional `merge_candidate`.

PDF ingestion validates its input and destination type, requires `pdftotext` or `marker`, rejects empty conversion output, stores normalized notes and metadata under `sources/<type>/<slug>/`, and splits content larger than 1 MiB into note parts.

The independent reviewer scopes its work to drafts matching the supplied source, persists one of `verified`, `needs-decision`, or `rejected` with evidence and notes, and reserves learner involvement for material merge, scope, or learning-priority exceptions rather than factual approval.

In a full run, `pipeline.py` executes `ingest` and `review`, then promotes only source-matching drafts persisted as `verified` and runs `topics` only after promotion succeeds; it skips both when none are verified, reports pending and needs-decision drafts as exceptions, retains rejected drafts, and treats unknown statuses as needs-decision. `lab` is available only as an explicit single step, and `--dry-run` does not run an agent.

The pipeline runner chooses the first configured agent for a role, expands environment variables in configuration strings and prompt placeholders, runs the assembled command with `shell=True` in `kb_root`, and treats a zero exit code as agent-process success. It does not sandbox agent writes, inspect diffs, or record learner decisions.

Promotion has a manual mode for one explicitly selected draft and a pipeline mode restricted to the exact supplied drafts that remain `review_status: verified`; a verified `merge_candidate` with clear reviewer rationale updates the existing concept, while an unclear merge is returned to `needs-decision`. First promotion defaults to depth 2, `lab_status: not-started`, and a review due date three days later.

Successful promotion maintains reciprocal related-concept links, adds at least two quiz entries, updates concept/tag/topic indexes as applicable, and removes the selected draft only after all required formal outputs and backlinks succeed; an incomplete promotion retains the draft.

Topics are curated learning paths over concepts with prerequisites and recommended order; the configured topics role updates an existing relevant path when possible, creates a new one only when no path covers the domain, and updates the topics index.

`index_generator.py` overwrites concept, topic, and tag indexes; concept and tag indexes intentionally include both canonical concepts and drafts, so index visibility is discovery information rather than proof of approval.

Labs are outside the default pipeline and require an explicit `lab` step; the learner must make predictions and fill the core before lab review, whose feedback may add next-day application quiz cards and update included concepts to `completed` or `explained`.

Weekly refinement can report stale drafts, overdue concepts, contradictions, questions, and missing-concept candidates, update quiz state and indexes, and append a refine log, but it is prohibited from modifying concepts or directly promoting drafts.

Metadata validation helpers report errors for unreadable or malformed YAML/frontmatter and missing required source, concept, or quiz fields, but their implementation checks required-field presence rather than semantic correctness or cross-record invariants.

The end-to-end test initializes a temporary vault, performs PDF ingestion using a mocked converter, validates normalized source metadata, supplies promoted concept and quiz fixtures, and verifies persisted quiz scheduling changes; it does not run the AI pipeline.

The lab-design workflow keeps the complete runnable lab in `~/orb_pods_share/<lab-id>/` and retains only `manifest.yaml` plus the canonical `spec.md` in `labs/<lab-id>/`; recovery uses those files to recreate equivalent learning behavior and acceptance criteria rather than byte-for-byte artifacts.

Lab generation is an ordered external-artifact workflow: it produces `spec.md`, then `spec.diataxis.md`, then a human review HTML artifact, and finally a dedicated Cloudflare Pages deployment; on unavailable Wrangler or authentication it must retain local HTML, record the blocker and retry commands, and not invent a review URL.

A lab requires only minimal recognition of the main term and its problem or expected input/output; `depth` and `lab_status` tune scaffold strength rather than block practice, and the public review surface must exclude learner predictions, expected answers, completed core solutions, secrets, and private URLs.

The topics role is a curation step over recently promoted concepts that reuses an existing path where possible and creates a new topic only when no path covers the domain; the normal full pipeline invokes it only after successful promotion, although `--step topics` remains directly callable.

Weekly refinement has a closed write scope: it may write the dated refine report, quiz bank, three discovery indexes, and an appended refine log, but it may not write drafts or topics in addition to its prohibition on changing concepts or directly promoting drafts.

A weekly refinement run may choose a five-to-ten-question review pack and regenerate indexes, but a report-only run may inspect quiz-bank format without arbitrarily changing schedules; result-driven updates must retain history and avoid overwriting unrelated questions.

Refinement findings about canonical corrections, merges, splits, or additions remain report recommendations for later independent evidence verification and the normal promotion workflow; insufficient evidence is marked as requiring more evidence, and only materially different alternatives may produce a needs-decision question.
